description: Add per-member brrr push notification onboarding and a separate scheduled reminder runner for Family Pulse. Phase 1 establishes secure channel registration, event subscription preferences, test delivery, and host-scheduled evaluation. Phase 2 adds concrete financial and technical reminder rules such as large expenses, sync failures, category budget overruns, and month-in-review nudges.

timing.gatingCondition: Can proceed immediately. Requires at least one real brrr webhook secret for end-to-end validation and a decision on whether Family Pulse should keep scheduled work in-process or move to a separate systemd timer runner.

principles: Notification delivery is opt-in per family member and parent-managed in settings
brrr secrets are write-only operational secrets stored in PostgreSQL, never in .env and never re-exposed after save
Detect reminder-worthy events on the server, not in the browser
Reminder evaluation runs outside the normal web request lifecycle
Keep channel delivery separate from event detection so future delivery options can reuse the same event engine
Prefer a small number of useful, trustworthy notifications over broad coverage that becomes spam
Every event type needs explicit dedupe and cooldown rules before it can ship
Deep links should land in an existing Pulse screen that helps the user act immediately

techStack.runtime: Express for settings and APIs, standalone Node runner for scheduled notification evaluation
techStack.database: PostgreSQL — notification channel storage, event subscriptions, reminder state/history
techStack.scheduler: systemd timer following the FamilyHelp pattern unless Family Pulse intentionally keeps in-process scheduling

executionStatus.mode: Planning only. Convert to active execution PRD once implementation starts and update slices/story status as code lands.
executionStatus.summary: Initial PRD drafted. The design deliberately mirrors FamilyHelp's brrr + systemd approach, but adapted to Family Pulse's household-member model and financial event triggers.
executionStatus.currentFocus: Define secure onboarding, event subscription semantics, and the first trustworthy reminder rules.
deferredForV1: Browser-native web push / PWA notification infrastructure
Digest batching across unrelated event types

phases.title: Notification Foundation + Onboarding
phases.goal: Users can securely register brrr targets, choose event categories, send a test notification, and rely on a separate runner foundation without yet enabling the full set of reminder rules.

phases.title: Financial + Technical Reminder Rules
phases.goal: Ship a small, trustworthy set of event rules with dedupe logic and deep links into existing Pulse screens.

userStories.title: Store per-member brrr notification channels securely
acceptanceCriteria: A family member can have zero or one active brrr channel in v1
The saved value can be either the raw secret or the full webhook URL and is normalized server-side
Secrets are stored in PostgreSQL, never in .env and never returned in full to the browser after save
Settings UI shows only masked state such as 'saved • ends in 9j0' and last-updated timestamp
Parents can add, replace, disable, enable, or clear a member's brrr channel
Kids cannot manage notification channels
userStories.testStrategy: node:test API coverage for save/replace/clear/mask/auth. Manual verification with one real secret and one full webhook URL.

userStories.title: Configure reminder subscriptions by event category per member
acceptanceCriteria: Settings page exposes simple event-category toggles per member
Initial event categories are: month_in_review, large_expense, sync_issue, budget_overrun
Subscriptions are separate from channel onboarding so a member can have a saved secret but no enabled event categories
Parents can configure subscriptions for parents only in v1
The storage model supports adding more event categories later without schema churn
userStories.testStrategy: node:test API coverage for CRUD and auth. Manual settings flow verification.

userStories.title: Provide a reusable brrr delivery helper and test-send endpoint
acceptanceCriteria: A small notification helper normalizes raw secret vs full webhook URL before sending
POST requests use JSON payloads matching the brrr docs
A parent-only test-send action can deliver a sample notification to a selected member without waiting for scheduled rules
Delivery failures are surfaced clearly in the UI and logged server-side without exposing secrets
The helper supports interruption-level and open_url because those are needed for Family Pulse event links
userStories.testStrategy: node:test for normalization and failure handling, plus manual real-device verification.

userStories.title: Scheduled notification runner with idempotent event evaluation
acceptanceCriteria: A standalone runner script evaluates notification candidates without requiring HTTP traffic
Runner can execute safely under a systemd timer following the FamilyHelp pattern
Runs are idempotent and do not re-send the same event to the same member inside a configured cooldown window
Runner logs what was considered, skipped, sent, and failed
A dry-run mode exists for validation without live delivery
If Family Pulse still keeps in-process sync scheduling, the notification runner remains separate from the web process regardless
userStories.testStrategy: Manual dry-run/live-run verification plus node:test helpers for cooldown logic.

userStories.title: Track reminder state and delivery history separately from source events
acceptanceCriteria: Reminder bookkeeping is not inferred from source tables alone
The system stores enough state to dedupe repeat sends by member, event type, and source entity or evaluation window
The last delivery attempt, last success time, and recent error state are queryable for operational debugging
State design supports both one-off alerts (large expense) and recurring cadence-based nudges (month in review)
Deleting or editing a notification channel does not corrupt event history
userStories.testStrategy: node:test for dedupe keys and repeated runner execution.

userStories.title: Large expense alert rule
acceptanceCriteria: A notification is eligible when a non-transfer, non-hidden, positive-amount expense transaction over a configurable threshold is first observed
Default threshold is $1,000
Pending transactions are excluded in v1 unless the household later decides otherwise
Each qualifying transaction can notify each subscribed member at most once
Notification deep-links to the transactions page filtered to the transaction or to its date context
Notification copy clearly distinguishes expense vs transfer-like events
userStories.testStrategy: node:test with seeded transactions covering transfer exclusion, hidden exclusion, pending exclusion, and one-time dedupe.

userStories.title: Sync failure / technical issue alert rule
acceptanceCriteria: A notification is eligible when sync enters a technical failure state or repeated failures persist beyond a short threshold
needs_reauth and sync_error are treated differently in copy and severity
Transient single-run failures can be suppressed if the next run succeeds quickly
Notification deep-links to Settings or the relevant management screen
A long-lived outage does not send a fresh push on every timer run; cooldown rules apply
userStories.testStrategy: node:test around import_runs/items state transitions plus repeated runner cycles.

userStories.title: Category budget overrun alert rule
acceptanceCriteria: A notification is eligible when a budget category first crosses a configurable percentage over its budget target for the current month
Default threshold is 15% over budget
Categories without a positive budget target are excluded
Each member receives at most one budget-overrun notification per category per period
Notification deep-links to Budget or filtered transactions for that category and month
The rule reuses existing budget summary / category overrun concepts instead of inventing a separate financial definition
userStories.testStrategy: node:test with seeded category budgets and month spending snapshots covering threshold crossing, below-threshold non-events, and one-time per-period dedupe.

userStories.title: Month-in-review reminder rule
acceptanceCriteria: A scheduled end-of-month or early-next-month reminder can nudge subscribed members to review the month
The notification links to Reports or another best available summary screen
At most one month-in-review reminder is sent per member per period
The copy remains useful even if a dedicated end-of-month report does not yet exist
userStories.testStrategy: Manual timer-date simulation and period-key dedupe verification.

high: Notification spam if event rules and cooldowns are not carefully constrained
Webhook secrets are sensitive operational secrets and must be masked everywhere outside the database write path
medium: Large-expense alerts may misfire on pending transactions, reimbursements, or unusual imported history if event sourcing is not scoped carefully
Systemd timer deployment must be coordinated with any existing in-process scheduling so duplicate runners are not introduced
low: brrr's intentionally simple webhook model is a good fit for Family Pulse's small-household scope
The FamilyHelp implementation already proves the basic secret storage and delivery model on the same host
operational: Need a clear admin-visible way to test a saved brrr target after entry
Need delivery logs or recent attempt state so a bad secret is debuggable without guessing
If the app later supports multiple devices per member, the current v1 single-channel simplification will need expansion
Budget-overrun alerts need a precise 'first crossing' definition so they do not fire repeatedly as spend inches upward

notes: Mirror FamilyHelp's channel table shape where useful, but keep Pulse-specific subscription state separate from delivery-channel rows.
Secrets should be stored write-only in the channel table; normal APIs return has_secret and secret_mask only.
notification_event_state should key dedupe by member_id, event_type, source_key, and the relevant period or transaction identifier.

settingsModel.audience: Parents manage parent notification settings in v1
notes: Store the Family Pulse base URL in config to build deep links that respect nginx/Tailscale deployment.
Keep the initial UI simple: one card per parent, one brrr channel, flat event category toggles.

cooldownExpectations: large_expense: once per qualifying transaction per member
sync_issue: once per incident window until recovered or cooldown expires
budget_overrun: once per category per month per member after the first threshold crossing
month_in_review: once per month per member

openQuestions: Should Family Pulse store one brrr channel per member in v1 or allow multiple devices/channels immediately?
Should pending transactions ever generate large-expense alerts after they post, and if so should the event key be the Plaid transaction ID?
Should month-in-review fire on the last day of the month, first day of the next month, or only after monthly-close/report generation exists?
Should technical alerts notify all subscribed parents or only one default operator first?
Should budget-overrun detection use only the category's primary budget target or also consider categories with very small budgets that would trigger too easily?
preFlightChecklist: Confirm the exact Family Pulse base URL/subpath for deep links in notifications
Review FamilyHelp's channel save/mask UX and reuse what maps cleanly
Decide whether Phase 1 includes a dedicated test-send button before any live event rules ship
Choose whether to keep the current in-process sync cron while introducing a separate notification runner, or whether both scheduler concerns should move to systemd together
Decide whether budget-overrun alerts should ignore tiny budget categories or rely entirely on the percentage threshold

executionSlices.name: Slice A: Schema + brrr delivery helper + test send
executionSlices.goal: Land secure channel storage and verify real-device delivery before any reminder logic exists.
notes: Add notification channel and subscription tables
Port and adapt FamilyHelp's brrr normalization helper
Add settings APIs for save/mask/clear/test-send
Add parent-only settings UI

executionSlices.name: Slice B: Runner foundation + systemd timer wiring
executionSlices.goal: Separate scheduled notification work from the web process and make evaluation repeatable and debuggable.
notes: Create standalone runner with dry-run mode
Add event state / delivery log tables
Add deploy units mirroring FamilyHelp's oneshot + timer pattern
Document operational workflow in README

executionSlices.name: Slice C: High-confidence rules first
executionSlices.goal: Ship the most obviously useful and least ambiguous event rules.
notes: Implement large expense rule
Implement sync issue rule
Implement budget overrun rule
Tune deep links and interruption levels
Verify cooldown behavior against repeated runner executions

executionSlices.name: Slice D: Softer cadence rules
executionSlices.goal: Add softer reminder categories after the high-confidence rules prove trustworthy.
notes: Implement month-in-review period reminder
Review notification fatigue before broadening scope
